diagram_math_checks.details: Each rectangle denotes the same connected cut-open complement Y, with copy indices n and n+1. The local Statement defines S_+ on the +n normal side and S_- on the -n normal side, and i_±: H_1(F;Z) -> H_1(Y;Z) through the face inclusion after j_*^{-1}. The seam label is exactly S_-(Y_n)=S_+(Y_{n+1}); it depicts the gluing in the Statement, not a different identification of signs.

The red arrow points from Y_n to Y_{n+1}, matching t in the Statement and proof step 2.1. That step fixes the normal via (n,k,u) positive, takes the meridian disk basis (u,n), and identifies positive crossing from the negative face of copy n to the positive face of copy n+1. No sign or index was reversed in this repair; the line is a schematic seam and the red arrow records the positive sheet shift.

For a class a in H_1(F), the seam contributes the negative-face image in copy n minus the positive-face image in copy n+1: t^n i_-(a)-t^(n+1)i_+(a)=t^n(i_- -t i_+)(a). This agrees with step 3.1. On connected H_0 the two face maps are identities and yield 1-t, also as in that step.

diagram_math_checks.check: Compatibility with the local Seifert matrix convention
diagram_math_checks.details: Read def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix and lem-knot-infinite-cyclic-cover-cut-and-paste-presentation. Here V_ij=lk(a_i^+,a_j). In linking-dual coordinates, the jth column of i_+ has ith entry lk(a_j^+,a_i)=V_ji, so i_+ has matrix V^T. For i_-, symmetry and a common positive collar translation give lk(a_j^-,a_i)=lk(a_i^+,a_j)=V_ij, so i_- has matrix V. Thus the preserved relation yields V-tV^T, exactly the local consumer convention; no generic alternative convention was substituted.

The existing numbered proof establishes the cut-space homology, cover, monodromy, and exact presentation without using the diagram. Only a TikZ library declaration changed, outside Facts and Proof in Remarks.
